target.title: fix(openai): reject malformed Codex image base64
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users generating images through the OpenAI Codex Responses route could receive a truncated or corrupted image when the SSE response contained malformed Base64 image data. Node's permissive decoder silently discarded invalid characters instead of surfacing the bad provider response.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Codex image decoder now trims the payload the same way Codex does, then validates and canonicalizes it with the existing media-runtime helper before decoding. The existing encoded-size limit is preserved and other OpenAI image routes are unchanged. The compatibility risk is limited to malformed Codex image results: inputs accepted by Codex's strict decoder remain accepted, including surrounding Unicode whitespace.

## User Impact

Malformed Codex image responses now fail with a clear provider-owned error instead of returning corrupted image bytes. Valid image responses continue to work normally.

## Evidence

Current dependency contract check: Codex `origin/main` at [`0fb559f`](https://github.com/openai/codex/commit/0fb559f0f6e231a88ac02ea002d3ecd248e2b515) models the image payload as the `result` string of an `image_generation_call` ([protocol model](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/0fb559f0f6e231a88ac02ea002d3ecd248e2b515/codex-rs/protocol/src/models.rs#L987-L1006)). Before saving, Codex applies `result.trim()` and decodes with `BASE64_STANDARD` ([decoder](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/0fb559f0f6e231a88ac02ea002d3ecd248e2b515/codex-rs/ext/image-generation/src/tool.rs#L230-L239)). Its workspace pins `base64` 0.22.1 ([dependency](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/0fb559f0f6e231a88ac02ea002d3ecd248e2b515/codex-rs/Cargo.toml#L282)); that crate's `STANDARD` engine requires the standard alphabet, canonical padding, and valid trailing bits ([configuration](https://github.com/marshallpierce/rust-base64/blob/v0.22.1/src/engine/general_purpose/mod.rs#L251-L263), [STANDARD engine](https://github.com/marshallpierce/rust-base64/blob/v0.22.1/src/engine/general_purpose/mod.rs#L331-L347)).

The proposed decoder now mirrors Codex's surrounding Unicode trim before calling OpenClaw's existing Base64 validator. That validator accepts the standard alphabet and canonical padding and is additionally tolerant of missing padding and ASCII whitespace, so this path is not stricter than Codex for valid standard-Base64 results. A committed positive regression test covers Codex-compatible surrounding Unicode whitespace, alongside malformed-payload tests for both terminal SSE event shapes.

Before/after behavior was exercised with a temporary local proof test that started a real `node:http` TCP server on `127.0.0.1`, returned Codex Responses SSE events, and called `buildOpenAIImageGenerationProvider().generateImage(...)` with the configured private-network opt-in. Only auth resolution used a fixed `test-token`; the production provider, SSRF handling, HTTP request, bounded SSE reader/parser, decoder, and result construction were used unchanged.

On current `upstream/main`, the malformed payload `aGVs!bG8=` was accepted and silently decoded to the five bytes for `hello`, so the negative assertion failed as expected:

```text
FAIL ... rejects malformed image data through real HTTP and SSE
AssertionError: promise resolved ... instead of rejecting
buffer data: [104, 101, 108, 108, 111]
Tests 1 failed | 1 skipped
```

With this change, the same real HTTP/SSE proof rejected the malformed payload while its valid Base64 control decoded to `hello`:

```text
✓ rejects malformed image data through real HTTP and SSE 241ms
✓ accepts valid image data through real HTTP and SSE 5ms
Test Files 1 passed (1)
Tests 2 passed (2)
```

Focused regression suite before the follow-up compatibility test:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/openai/image-generation-provider.test.ts
Test Files 1 passed (1)
Tests 71 passed (71)
```

Additional checks: targeted `oxfmt`, targeted `oxlint`, and `git diff --check` passed. `autoreview --mode uncommitted` reported no accepted/actionable findings (`patch is correct`, confidence `0.96`). The follow-up commit passed `git diff --check`; full validation, including its committed Unicode-whitespace regression, is running in GitHub Actions. Live OpenAI credentials were not available, so no request was sent to the hosted provider.

AI-assisted: Codex helped implement and review this change; the source inspection and all evidence above were run manually.
